payload.contract: Find unique integers in encounter order. Input can contain millions of distinct integers. Report unmeasured complexity as an advisory.

candidates.title: Quadratic membership search during encounter-order deduplication
candidates.description: In subject.py, unique(items) performs linear search `if value not in result:` on a list that grows up to n elements. For an input iterable with n distinct items, iteration i inspects up to i elements, resulting in Theta(n^2) value comparisons. A linear alternative using an auxiliary seen set (`seen = set()`, checking `if value not in seen:` and performing `seen.add(value)`) or `list(dict.fromkeys(items))` reduces comparisons to O(n) hash operations while preserving encounter order and returning a materialized list of unique elements.
candidates.impact: Repeated scanning across the accumulating result list yields quadratic comparison growth rather than linear growth for distinct integers, scaling poorly as input size reaches millions of items.
candidates.remediation: Track visited values in an auxiliary set (`seen = set()`) alongside `result`, checking `if value not in seen: seen.add(value); result.append(value)`, or return `list(dict.fromkeys(items))` to deduplicate in linear time while preserving encounter order.
